To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the application rate of the herbicide is a critical determinant for the efficacy of the treatment.

the use of a high‐pressure spray nozzle, a large‐diameter spray boom, and a large‐area spray fan, combined with the use of a small‐volume carrier fluid and a low carrier‐to‐pesticide volume ratio, will result in the production of a spray cloud containing a high percentage of fine droplets.
The use of a low‐cost, portable device for measuring droplet size and velocity can provide useful information to improve the performance of aerial spray applications in forestry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new analytical and experimental techniques for the study of the physical properties and behavior of pesticides and other agrochemicals.
the development of a new approach to the design and control of the spray process in the application of pesticides to the forest canopy.
the development and testing of a new approach to the design of insecticide application equipment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of pesticides in the field is a function of the physical and chemical properties of the pesticide and the physical properties of the spray mixture.

, in forestry, the most important factors affecting the performance of pesticides are: (1) the nature and amount of the active ingredient, (2) the type and size of the droplets used, and (3) the environmental conditions at the time of application.

, in order to obtain maximum efficiency of pesticide application, the following factors should be taken into consideration: (1) the physical properties of the chemical; (2) the nature of the target; (3) the environmental factors, such as wind, temperature, humidity, etc.; (4) the type of equipment used; and (5) the skill and experience of the operator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of pesticides in forest management is a highly specialized field that requires knowledge of the pest and the forest environment.

the physical factors that affect the performance of pesticides in the forest environment can be classified into four groups: 1) factors related to the physical properties of the pesticide, 2) factors related to spray application, 3) factors related to environmental conditions, and 4) factors related to target organisms.
the use of the spray volume and the emission rate used in the field is the key factor for the droplet size produced, which is a major factor for the coverage of the target area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of pesticides in agriculture is not only a matter of economic efficiency but a matter of social justice and environmental sustainability.

the physical factors that affect insecticide performance in forests are the same as those that affect insecticide use in other crops, but the magnitude of the effect of these factors may be different.
we can use the physical properties of the pesticide to predict the environmental fate of the pesticide.
